en: The Jātaka: The Fifth Book of Birth Stories (Pañcakanipāta),
Chapter on the Half (Aḍḍhavagga)
1. The Dīghīti Kosala Jātaka “O King,
since you have come under my power in such a state, [what will you do?]”
“Is there any means,
my dear, that might release you from this suffering? “For one who has become such as I am, father...”
It is now under your power as you have arrived;
there is no means whatsoever for us by which you might release me from this suffering.
“Nothing else is well-practiced,
O King, nothing else is well-spoken;
only these protect one at the time of death.”
In the same way, one should regard other wealth:
"He has insulted me, he has struck me,
he has defeated me, he has taken away my possessions."
And those who harbor resentment toward such a person find that their enmity does not subside.
"He abused me, he struck me," [they think].
"He has conquered me, he has defeated me";
yet for those who do not harbor resentment toward him,
their enmity is stilled.
For never in this world are hostilities stilled by hostility;
they are stilled by non-hostility.
“This is the eternal law.
The first story, the Dīghīti Kosala Jātaka.
